facts.statement: Eosqualiolus is an extinct genus of sharks belonging to the family Dalatiidae.
facts.quote: Eosqualiolus is an extinct genus of sharks in the family Dalatiidae.

facts.statement: The genus Eosqualiolus was first described by Sylvain Adnet in 2006.
facts.quote: It was described by Sylvain Adnet in 2006

facts.statement: The type species, E. aturensis, lived during the middle Eocene in what is now France.
facts.quote: the type species is E. aturensis, which existed during the middle Eocene of what is now France

facts.statement: The species E. skrovinai was described by Charlie J. Underwood and Jan Schlogl in 2012 from fossils found in Slovakia during the Miocene.
facts.quote: A new species, E. skrovinai, which existed in what is now Slovakia during the Miocene period, was described by Charlie J. Underwood and Jan Schlogl in 2012

facts.statement: The species E. skrovinai was identified based on 14 fossil teeth discovered in the Laksarska Nova Ves Formation.
facts.quote: E. skrovinai was described from 14 fossil teeth found in the Laksarska Nova Ves Formation

facts.statement: Eosqualiolus fossils date from the Lutetian to the Burdigalian stages, between 48.07 and 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Burdigalian (48.07 to 15.98 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eosqualiolus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
